A verbalized confidence baseline confirms that score compression is not LP-specific: the model's self-rated confidence (mean 8.6/10) is even more compressed and yields the weakest selection despite higher $\rho$ than LP (Appendix~\ref{app:verbalized_confidence}; \citealp{bhattacharyya2026beyond}).

\paragraph{Hypotheses for LP compression.}

We identify four (non-mutually-exclusive) mechanisms that may explain within-instance LP compression, though we do not isolate their individual contributions:
(a) \textit{token-level averaging}---mean log-probability over long sequences smooths token-level variance, compressing the effective signal;
(b) \textit{schema-dominated tokens}---constrained decoding enforces structural tokens (brackets, type labels) that carry no extraction information yet dominate the sequence, reducing effective variance; and
(c) \textit{vocabulary restriction}---constrained decoding shrinks the effective vocabulary at each step, concentrating probability mass and reducing log-probability variation; and
(d) \textit{format-token dilution}---fine-tuned models assign extremely high LP to schema tokens (\texttt{\{"entities": [}~etc.) that carry no extraction information, diluting the signal from entity-name tokens; free-form parse rates of 99.95\% confirm that format tokens dominate the sequence.
Mechanisms (b)--(c) predict that free-form decoding should reduce compression; our NER ablation finds negligible change (std ratio 0.97; Appendix~\ref{app:freeform_ablation}), suggesting (a) and (d) are the primary drivers for NER.

1	\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	We evaluate five confidence signals for quality estimation and sample selection in LLM-based NER, revealing the \textit{correlation-selection gap}: moderate-to-strong quality estimation ($\rho{=}0.38$ on medium-difficulty NER, up to 0.45 on a ceiling-effect control) coexists with selection that fails to outperform cost-free greedy decoding.
4	The gap stems from two mechanisms: instance degeneracy (21--58\% of instances produce identical F1 across all $N$ samples, eliminating selection headroom despite positive within-instance utility correlation) and LP compression (the only per-sample signal has median within-instance range of 0.041 nats).
5	Diagnostic ablations---free-form decoding, entity-token LP isolation---confirm compression is intrinsic rather than an artifact of constrained decoding or format-token dilution.
6	The gap is demonstrated in the medium-difficulty regime where models achieve moderate but imperfect accuracy; signal rankings shift with difficulty and collapse at the capability boundary in the small-model regime (3B--8B).
7	Whether these mechanisms persist at 70B+ scales is an open question; trained verifiers and an exploratory extension to relation extraction (Appendix~\ref{app:re_extension}) are promising directions.
